idiom_name: tagged union (tag + payload union) + total matcher
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: declare one type carrying exactly one of several alternatives. Each alternative has a constructor taking its own product of fields; the value stores a tag recording which constructor was used plus that constructor's payload. Provide one eliminator (match/switch/visit) with a branch per alternative and require it to cover all of them - the language's exhaustiveness check, a linter, or a test that enumerates the set is the enforcement mechanism. Keep the plain constructors total and put validation into smart constructors so every constructed value is legal. Where the language has a native sum type (enum with payload, sealed hierarchy, discriminated union) the tag and the coverage check are generated for you; the hand-written form remains for C, Go-style interfaces and other languages without a closed-set type.
code_sketch:
type Value = A(a1, a2) | B(b1) | C          # one tag, one payload per constructor

v = A(x, y)                                  # construction: exactly one alternative
match v:                                     # elimination: one branch per alternative
    case A(a1, a2): use(a1, a2)
    case B(b1):     use(b1)
    case C:         skip()                   # no wildcard: a new variant must fail here
pitfalls: Wrong move: expose a mutable tag beside a free-standing payload union -> Failure: callers can change the tag without changing the payload, so reads interpret the wrong fields -> Instead: construct each case through a constructor or smart constructor that couples its tag to its product.

Wrong move: add a wildcard or default arm to an internal eliminator -> Failure: adding a case still compiles and silently routes it through fallback behaviour -> Instead: list every closed case and reserve a wildcard for foreign or intentionally open data.

Wrong move: model optionality by adding nullable fields to one case -> Failure: combinations such as both fields set or neither set become representable again -> Instead: make each legal combination its own variant with a case-specific product.
